attestations.source_text:
Reflexive verbs
The action of a reflexive verb is, for the most part, reflected back on the subject, the action being done to oneself.
The second type of pronominal verb is called reciprocal. It describes an action two or more people perform with or for each other.
A third type of pronominal verb is called passive. With the passive pronominal verbs, the subject is not a person or an animal.
The last type of pronominal verb is called subjective. These verbs are neither reflexive nor reciprocal.

concepts.name: Pronominal verbs
concepts.description: Verbs preceded by me, te, se, nous, vous, se in infinitive and conjugated forms.

attestations.source_text: Pronominal verbs are verbs that are preceded in the infinitive and in conjugated forms by the pronouns me, te, se, nous, vous, se.

concepts.name: Reflexive verbs
concepts.description: Action reflected back on the subject.

attestations.source_text: The action of a reflexive verb is, for the most part, reflected back on the subject, the action being done to oneself.

concepts.name: Reciprocal verbs
concepts.description: Action two or more people perform with or for each other.

attestations.source_text: It describes an action two or more people perform with or for each other.

concepts.name: Passive pronominal
concepts.description: Subject not person or animal; action performed on subject; used in 3rd person singular with se.

attestations.source_text: With the passive pronominal verbs, the subject is not a person or an animal. The subject does not perform the action of the verb but rather is subjected to it. It is in the third-person singular, with se.

concepts.name: Subjective pronominal
concepts.description: Idiomatic or historical use of pronominal form; neither reflexive nor reciprocal.

attestations.source_text: These verbs are neither reflexive nor reciprocal. For idiomatic or historical reasons, they just happen to use the pronominal forms.

concepts.name: Imperative with pronominal verbs
concepts.description: Affirmative: verb + stressed pronoun (toi/nous/vous). Negative: ne + pronoun + verb + pas.

attestations.section_title: Pronominals in the imperative and the infinitive
attestations.source_text: For the affirmative imperative, add the stressed pronoun toi, nous, or vous after the verb, connected with a hyphen. For the negative imperative, use ne in front of the pronoun and pas after the verb.

concepts.name: Pronominal verbs with infinitive
concepts.description: Reflexive pronoun agrees with subject and precedes infinitive.

attestations.section_title: Pronominals in the imperative and the infinitive
attestations.source_text: When pronominal verbs are used in the infinitive, the reflexive pronoun is always in the same person and number as the subject, and it precedes the infinitive.

grammar_rules.summary: Pronominal verbs are preceded by me, te, se, nous, vous, se in infinitive and conjugated forms.
grammar_rules.explanation: Pronominal verbs are verbs that are preceded in the infinitive and in conjugated forms by the pronouns me, te, se, nous, vous, se.
agreement_rules: Reflexive pronoun agrees with subject in person and number.
grammar_rules.word_order: Pronoun before verb in normal sentences.
grammar_rules.interrogative_form: Rising intonation, est-ce que, or inversion; pronoun remains before verb in inversion.
common_traps: Do not drop the reflexive pronoun.

attestations.source_text: Pronominal verbs are verbs that are preceded in the infinitive and in conjugated forms by the pronouns me, te, se, nous, vous, se.

grammar_rules.summary: Me, te, se drop e before mute h or vowel.
grammar_rules.explanation: The pronouns me, te, se drop the e before mute h or a vowel.
grammar_rules.formation: me → m', te → t', se → s'

attestations.source_text: The pronouns me, te, se drop the e before mute h or a vowel.

grammar_rules.summary: ne follows subject pronoun; pas follows conjugated verb.
grammar_rules.explanation: In the negative form, the ne follows the subject pronoun and the pas follows the conjugated verb.
common_traps: Do not place ne after the pronoun.

attestations.source_text: In the negative form, the ne follows the subject pronoun and the pas follows the conjugated verb.

grammar_rules.summary: Three ways: rising intonation, est-ce que, inversion; pronoun remains before verb.
grammar_rules.explanation: In the interrogative form, there are three ways of asking questions. Rising intonation (Tu te couches déjà?). With inversion, the reflexive pronoun remains in front of the verb. Also est-ce que.
grammar_rules.formation: Rising intonation: Tu te couches? ; Inversion: Te couches-tu? ; Est-ce que: Est-ce que tu te couches?
common_traps: In inversion, keep pronoun before verb.

attestations.source_text: In the interrogative form, there are three ways of asking questions. You can always make a question with rising intonation (Tu te couches déjà?). When inversion is used, the reflexive pronoun remains in front of the verb.

grammar_rules.summary: Action between two or more people; used in plural only.
grammar_rules.explanation: Reciprocal verbs describe an action two or more people perform with or for each other. Since two or more people are involved, reciprocal verbs can only be used in the plural (with se, nous, vous).
common_traps: Do not use singular forms for reciprocal meaning.

attestations.source_text: The second type of pronominal verb is called reciprocal. It describes an action two or more people perform with or for each other. Since two or more people are involved, reciprocal verbs can only be used in the plural (with se, nous, vous).

grammar_rules.summary: Subject not person/animal; verb in 3rd person singular with se; expresses passive meaning.
grammar_rules.explanation: With passive pronominal verbs, the subject does not perform the action but is subjected to it. It is in the third-person singular, with se.
restrictions: Subject is not a person or animal.

attestations.source_text: With the passive pronominal verbs, the subject is not a person or an animal. The subject does not perform the action of the verb but rather is subjected to it. It is in the third-person singular, with se.

grammar_rules.summary: Idiomatic pronominal verbs; learn with se; not reflexive or reciprocal.
grammar_rules.explanation: These verbs are neither reflexive nor reciprocal. For idiomatic or historical reasons, they just happen to use the pronominal forms. Learn their infinitives with the pronoun se.

attestations.source_text: The last type of pronominal verb is called subjective. These verbs are neither reflexive nor reciprocal. For idiomatic or historical reasons, they just happen to use the pronominal forms. Try to learn their infinitives with the pronoun se.

grammar_rules.summary: Add stressed pronoun after verb with hyphen.
grammar_rules.explanation: For the affirmative imperative, add the stressed pronoun toi, nous, or vous after the verb, connected with a hyphen.

attestations.section_title: Pronominals in the imperative and the infinitive
attestations.source_text: For the affirmative imperative, add the stressed pronoun toi, nous, or vous after the verb, connected with a hyphen.

grammar_rules.explanation: For the negative imperative, use ne in front of the pronoun and pas after the verb. The reflexive pronoun precedes the verb, as in a normal sentence.
common_traps: Do not place pronoun after verb in negative imperative.

attestations.section_title: Pronominals in the imperative and the infinitive
attestations.source_text: For the negative imperative of pronominal verbs, use ne in front of the pronoun and pas after the verb. Note that in the negative the reflexive pronoun precedes the verb, as it would in a normal sentence.

grammar_rules.summary: Reflexive pronoun agrees with subject and precedes infinitive.
grammar_rules.explanation: When pronominal verbs are used in the infinitive, the reflexive pronoun is always in the same person and number as the subject, and it precedes the infinitive.
usage: After verbs like aller, venir de, devoir, pouvoir, aimer, etc.
common_traps: Do not forget the pronoun before infinitive.

attestations.section_title: Pronominals in the imperative and the infinitive
attestations.source_text: When pronominal verbs are used in the infinitive, the reflexive pronoun is always in the same person and number as the subject, and it precedes the infinitive.
